clue.text: Mackenzie's book is fair entertainment

definitions.meaning: Compton Mackenzie wrote a 1912 novel of that title about a dancer
the merriment and rides of a fair or festival

explanation.surface: A reviewer notes that a novelist's book makes pleasant, fair-minded reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' reads as 'reasonably good' but means a funfair. Compton Mackenzie was a Scottish novelist of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is a novel's title; the second is a festive fun-fair with processions and amusements.

clue.text: Rome's general farmer ?

definitions.meaning: the Roman governor of Britain whose life Tacitus wrote
the Latin word for a tiller of fields

explanation.surface: A Roman military leader was also a farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus's father-in-law commanded Roman forces in Britain, and his name is the Latin noun for a cultivator of fields.

clue.text: Up again, far up, everything's there for splashdown

indicators.note: up means stirred or in disorder, so the letters of again and far are mixed

parts.note: all's is a contraction of all is, everything is

explanation.surface: A spacecraft is lifted again after everything is ready for a sea landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splashdown' suggests a capsule landing at sea; here it is the plunge of water. AGAINFAR rearranged gives NIAGARAF.
explanation.definitionFit: The great waterfalls on the US-Canada border are where water crashes down, and daredevils splash down in barrels.

clue.text: Sailors gave rosy versions

indicators.note: versions are variant forms, so the letters of the two words are given a new order

explanation.surface: Seamen tell optimistic accounts of their trips.
explanation.definitionFit: People on sea journeys, sea travellers.

clue.text: Principal cricket side includes a big noise

indicators.note: includes tells us the side of the field takes the next two pieces inside it

parts.note: leg is the side of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs, also called on side
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A leading cricket team has a self-important bigwig in its ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big noise' seems to mean an important person, but here is just DIN. LEG is one half of a cricket field.
explanation.definitionFit: Principal as an adjective means chief or foremost, the most important.

clue.text: Begin again with the summary

definitions.meaning: a short account, also spelt with accents in French

explanation.surface: Restarting after a recap of what went before.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means take up again; as a noun it is a précis.

clue.text: Assent to change of name ?

indicators.note: change of tells us the letters of the following word are altered in order

explanation.surface: Agreeing to a new name, perhaps after marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word said at the end of a prayer means 'so be it', an expression of agreement.

clue.text: Moneylender almost as afterthought releases his hold

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: uncle is slang for a pawnbroker
taken as written
PS, postscript, is an afterthought at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A loan shark, as an afterthought, lets go of his grip on a borrower.
explanation.walkthrough: The pawnbroker is called 'uncle' in old slang; 'almost' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfastening a clasp or grip, so letting go.

clue.text: Anybody's hero in play

parts.note: the medieval morality play whose title figure stands for any ordinary person

explanation.surface: Any member of the audience might be the hero of the drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth-century morality play's protagonist represents all mankind, so the name means the typical ordinary person.

clue.text: Song needs a melody backing

indicators.note: backing means the word for the tune is written back to front after the A

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A singer's number calls for a tune with accompaniment behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' poses as musical accompaniment but turns AIR round to RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic solo piece is a kind of song.

clue.text: Puppet jolly good in horror plays

parts.note: grand is an informal word for excellent
Guignol is the chief character of the French puppet show, like Punch

explanation.surface: A puppet show that is great fun appears among some gruesome dramas.
explanation.walkthrough: Guignol is the Lyon puppet who plays the part Punch plays in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris theatre of that name staged gory melodramas, so the term names macabre theatrical entertainment.

clue.text: Ten-dollar birds

definitions.meaning: old US gold coins worth ten dollars were called eagles
large brown birds of prey of mountains

explanation.surface: Birds costing ten dollars apiece.
explanation.definitionFit: The ten-dollar US gold coin was an eagle, so gold ones are those coins; the same words name large raptors.

clue.text: Where French exchange rates would be about ours ?

indicators.note: about tells us the two letters of the first word go round the second word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The French rate of exchange would be about the same as our own.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'where French exchange rates [are fixed]'; 'would' is a link, and 'be about ours' places B and E either side of OURS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris stock market is the place where shares and currencies are priced.

clue.text: Something to say that's obvious

parts.note: the stock phrase used to introduce a remark that hardly needs making

explanation.surface: A remark so plain it need hardly be made.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is completed by the idiom: the word, followed by 'to say', means 'obviously'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom meaning 'of course' is formed by this word plus 'to say', so the word introduces an obvious remark.

clue.text: Fast-looking from a service angle

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services
to angle is to fish with a rod and line

explanation.surface: Something seems speedy when viewed from a particular military viewpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angle' suggests a viewpoint but is the verb for fishing. 'Fast' here means loose-living, not quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rakish or dissolute in appearance looks disreputable and pleasure-seeking, the old sense of fast.

clue.text: These go along with the slogan " They shall not pass "

definitions.text: These go along with the slogan " They shall not pass "

parts.words: These go along with the slogan " They shall not pass "
parts.note: the First World War defiant cry is reread as the attitude of selfish drivers blocking overtakers

explanation.surface: Followers of a famous wartime battle cry of defiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They shall not pass' was the French rallying cry at Verdun; here 'go along' means travel the road, and 'pass' means overtake.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfish motorists who hog the road refuse to let others overtake them.

clue.text: Cassius' scene to be re-enacted " in states unborn, and yet unknown

definitions.text: Cassius' scene to be re-enacted " in states unborn, and yet unknown

parts.words: Cassius' scene to be re-enacted " in states unborn, and yet unknown
parts.note: a gap-fill from Julius Caesar, where Cassius foresees the assassination acted again in nations and languages yet to exist

explanation.surface: Cassius predicts that the murder of Caesar will be performed again in future lands.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, Act 3, Cassius says the lofty scene will be acted over 'in states unborn and accents yet unknown'; the clue's dash marks the missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in the quotation means tongues or ways of speaking, here languages not yet spoken.

clue.text: Something topping, music variations, hot stuff !

parts.note: a cap is something that sits on top

indicators.note: variations are altered versions, so the letters of the word are reordered

explanation.surface: Excellent tunes in new arrangements are a sizzling success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' suggests 'excellent' but is literal: a cap goes on top. 'variations' rearranges MUSIC as SICUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The pepper genus includes chillies, which are fiery to taste.

clue.text: Herb Paris names for his sweetheart ?

definitions.meaning: a woodland plant with four leaves round one berry

explanation.surface: A man named Herb picks names for his girlfriend from Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb Paris' looks like a man called Herb in Paris, but it is the plant Paris quadrifolia, also known by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The four-leaved woodland plant Paris quadrifolia has this folk name, which also means a beloved.

clue.text: Present on Market Day

parts.note: a gift bought at a fair, which takes place on a market day

explanation.surface: Attending on the day the market is held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like 'attending' but means a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift bought at a fair or market, traditionally a sweet or trinket.

clue.text: Newman's vindication of early sayings on a river

indicators.note: on means the sayings are placed after the earlier pieces in this across answer

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
logia are the collected sayings attributed to Jesus in early Christian texts

explanation.surface: Cardinal Newman defends his account of old sayings found beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: John Henry Newman wrote Apologia Pro Vita Sua (1864) defending his religious life.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin title of Newman's book means a formal written defence of one's opinions or conduct.

clue.text: State wagon for a chivalrous knight

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
a wain is an old word for a farm wagon

explanation.surface: An official carriage of state arrives for a gallant knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State wagon' suggests a ceremonial coach; it is GA plus WAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Gawain of Arthurian legend, hero of the Green Knight tale, is a model of courtesy.

clue.text: Per this a network would bewilder us

definitions.text: Per this a network would bewilder us

parts.words: Per this a network would bewilder us
parts.note: putting the syllable per before the word for a network makes a phrase meaning confuse us

explanation.surface: With this per-unit system, a broadcasting network would confuse its audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Put PER in front of the answer and it reads 'perplex us', that is, bewilder us; the answer itself means a network of nerves or vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: A plexus is an anatomical web of interlaced nerves or blood vessels, an intricate network.

clue.text: Party at Westminster getting steamed up ?

parts.note: the House of Commons and House of Lords sit at Westminster
warming is heating up, as something steamed would be

explanation.surface: A political party in Parliament is becoming heated and angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a political party at Westminster, but it is the celebration held when moving into a new home.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebration for friends given on moving into a new home is a kind of party.

clue.text: Runs amok with samovars

indicators.note: running amok is going wild, so the letters of the word go wild

explanation.surface: Someone charges around in a frenzy carrying tea urns.
explanation.definitionFit: A samovar is a Russian tea vessel, a kind of large container for heating water.

clue.text: The bird's a rascal

definitions.meaning: a large diving waterbird, called a diver in Britain
a Scots word for a worthless fellow or rogue

explanation.surface: A bird of bad character.
explanation.definitionFit: The diving waterbird shares its name with an old Scottish term for a scamp or idler.

clue.text: The band celebrity is the nerve-centre

parts.note: a gang is a band of people
a lion is a famous person, as in a literary lion

explanation.surface: The group's star performer is the heart of the operation.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'lion' is an old word for a celebrity, as in 'social lion'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cluster of nerve cells, and figuratively a hub of activity.

clue.text: He's willing to ruin the rest, to play his hunch

definitions.text: He's willing to ruin the rest, to play his hunch

parts.note: game means ready and willing, as in game for anything

indicators.note: to ruin is to wreck, so the letters of the following word are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A gambler will happily bankrupt everyone else to back his instinct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ruin' scrambles REST into STER after GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler risks everything on a feeling, even at the cost of others.
